_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for tax-year figures. Pages reference keys via <Figure id="..."/>. Update here each fall when the IRS releases inflation adjustments; every page updates. Each entry: value, taxYear, source (Rev. Proc. / IRC / IRS page), verified (date).

oic.application_fee.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet

ia.setup_fee.online_directdebit.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.online_other.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.phone_mail_directdebit.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.phone_mail_other.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.lowincome.value: waived with direct debit; $43 otherwise, reimbursed on completion
ia.setup_fee.lowincome.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b); IRC § 6159(f)

penalty.ftf.rate.value: 5% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 25%

penalty.ftp.rate.value: 0.5% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 25%

penalty.ftf.minimum.value: the lesser of $535 or 100% of the tax required to be shown, for returns required to be filed in 2027
penalty.ftf.minimum.source: IRC § 6651(a) flush language and § 6651(j); Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.52

penalty.fraud.rate.value: 75% of the underpayment attributable to fraud

preparer.6694a.value: the greater of $1,000 or 50% of the income derived or to be derived from the return or claim

preparer.6694b.value: the greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income derived or to be derived from the return or claim

sol.assessment.general.value: 3 years from the later of the due date or the date filed

sol.assessment.substantial_omission.value: 6 years (omission exceeding 25% of the gross income stated on the return)

sol.refund.general.value: later of 3 years from filing or 2 years from payment

cdp.response_days.value: 30 days — for a lien, beginning the day after the 5-business-day period following the NFTL filing; for a levy, the 30-day period after the final notice

records.general_retention.value: as long as the period of limitations for the return runs; employment tax records at least 4 years after the tax is due or paid, whichever is later
records.general_retention.source: IRC § 6001; IRS Pub. 583, How Long To Keep Records (page reviewed 30 April 2026)

preparer.records_retention_6107.value: 3 years after the close of the return period — a completed copy, or a list of taxpayer names and identifying numbers

ea.ce.hours_per_cycle.value: 72 hours per enrollment cycle including 6 hours of ethics, and a minimum of 16 hours per enrollment year including 2 hours of ethics

ptin.fee.value: $18.75 to apply or renew — a $10 annual IRS fee plus $8.75 charged by the contractor
ptin.fee.source: Reg. § 300.11 (applies from 30 September 2025); irs.gov PTIN requirements page

ia.short_term.fee.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.short_term.max_days.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.simple.threshold.value: $50,000 or less aggregate unpaid balance of assessment

oic.lump_sum_initial.value: 20% of the total offer, with the application
oic.lump_sum_initial.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet; IRC § 7122(c)(1)(A)

oic.lump_sum_max_payments.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet; IRC § 7122(c)(1)(A)(ii)

preparer.6695.per_failure.value: $65 per return or claim, capped at $33,000
preparer.6695.per_failure.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(a)–(e)

preparer.6695f.check.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(f)

preparer.6695g.duediligence.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(g)

preparer.6694a.assessment_period.value: 3 years from the filing of the return or claim

preparer.6694b.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — assessable at any time

preparer.stay_of_collection.value: 15% of the penalty, paid within 30 days of notice and demand, with a refund claim

penalty.accuracy.gross_valuation.value: 40% of the underpayment attributable to a gross valuation misstatement

penalty.substantial_understatement.thres.value: an understatement exceeding the greater of 10% of the tax required to be shown or $5,000 (corporations: the lesser of the greater of 10% or $10,000, or $10,000,000)

penalty.frivolous.value: $5,000 per frivolous return or specified frivolous submission

preparer.6701.individual.value: $1,000 per document, and only one penalty per person per taxpayer per taxable period

preparer.6701.corporate.value: $10,000 per document where the document relates to a corporation's tax liability

preparer.6713.per_disclosure.value: $250 per disclosure or use, capped at $10,000 per calendar year

preparer.7216.criminal.value: a misdemeanor: a fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment of up to one year, or both, plus costs of prosecution

penalty.valuation.thresholds.value: substantial at 150% or more of the correct value or adjusted basis; gross at 200% or more

preparer.6695B.assessment_period.value: 6 years from the filing of the return or claim

preparer.6713.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — § 6696(d) does not reach § 6713

preparer.refund_claim_period.value: 3 years from the date the penalty was paid

preparer.suit_window.value: 30 days after the earlier of denial of the refund claim or the expiration of 6 months from filing it

preparer.consent_windows.value: a consent is sought when under 180 days remain, and must be obtained if the case goes to Appeals with under 365 days remaining

circ230.10_51.categories.value: 18 enumerated categories, expressly a non-exhaustive list

circ230.monetary_penalty.cap.value: not more than the gross income derived, or to be derived, from the conduct giving rise to the penalty

circ230.standard_of_proof.value: preponderance of the evidence for censure or suspension under six months; clear and convincing evidence for a monetary penalty, disbarment, or suspension of six months or longer

circ230.answer.min_days.value: not less than 30 days from service of the complaint

circ230.alj.decision_days.value: 180 days after the hearing closes and proposed findings are received

circ230.appeal.days.value: 30 days from service of the Administrative Law Judge decision

circ230.agency_decision.days.value: 180 days after receipt of the appeal

circ230.reinstatement.period.value: 5 years after disbarment, suspension or disqualification, or immediately after a shorter period expires

circ230.expedited.lookback.value: conduct within the 5 years before the show cause order is served

circ230.expedited.nonfiling.value: no annual return in 4 of the 5 preceding tax years, or no more-frequent return in 5 of the 7 preceding tax periods, and still noncompliant when the suspension notice issues

efile.specified_preparer.threshold.value: a preparer who does not reasonably expect to file 10 or fewer individual income tax returns in the calendar year — that is, 11 or more, counted across the firm

efile.waiver_window.value: between 1 October of the preceding calendar year and 15 February of the applicable calendar year

efile.waiver_duration.value: not ordinarily granted for more than a one calendar year period

efile.1040x.periods.value: the current tax period and the two prior ones

frivolous.positions.count.value: 46 numbered positions, each covering positions that are the same as or similar to it
frivolous.positions.count.source: Notice 2010-33, § III (effective for submissions made and issues raised after 7 April 2010)

frivolous.withdrawal_window.value: 30 days after the IRS notifies the person that a submission is a specified frivolous submission

frivolous.tax_court_penalty.value: up to $25,000 imposed by the Tax Court, and up to $10,000 in a section 7433 proceeding in another court

fraud.civil.standard.value: clear and convincing evidence, the burden resting on the government

fraud.criminal.standard.value: beyond a reasonable doubt, the burden resting on the government

fraud.ftf.rate.value: 15% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 75%

fraud.7201.sentence.value: a felony: a fine of up to $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation), imprisonment of up to 5 years, or both, plus costs of prosecution

fraud.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — tax may be assessed at any time on a false or fraudulent return filed with intent to evade

preparer.6060.return_period.value: the 12-month period beginning on 1 July each year

preparer.6060.retention.value: 3 years following the close of the return period to which the record relates

duediligence.retention.value: 3 years from the latest of the unextended due date, the e-filing date, the date presented to the taxpayer for signature, or a nonsigning preparer's submission date

duediligence.benefits.value: head of household filing status; the child tax credit, additional child tax credit and credit for other dependents under section 24; the American opportunity tax credit; and the earned income credit

lien.release_days.value: not later than 30 days after the liability is satisfied or becomes legally unenforceable, or a bond is accepted

lien.refiling_period.value: the one-year period ending 30 days after the expiration of 10 years from the date of assessment, and each 10-year period after that

lien.cdp_notice_days.value: within 5 business days after the notice of lien is filed, with the 30-day hearing window opening the day after that period

levy.notice_days.value: no less than 30 days before the levy, given in person, left at the dwelling or usual place of business, or sent by certified or registered mail to the last known address

levy.demand_days.value: 10 days after notice and demand, unless collection is in jeopardy

levy.exempt.household.value: $11,980 of fuel, provisions, furniture, household personal effects, arms for personal use, livestock and poultry

levy.exempt.tools.value: $5,990 of books and tools necessary for the taxpayer's trade, business or profession

levy.exempt.small_residence.value: any residence where the amount of the levy does not exceed $5,000

levy.continuous.federal_payments.value: up to 15% of a specified federal payment, continuous until released

levy.redemption.value: 180 days after the sale, on payment of the purchase price plus interest at 20% per annum

csed.period.value: 10 years after the assessment of the tax

csed.cdp_tail.value: suspended while a CDP hearing and appeals are pending, and in no event expiring before the 90th day after a final determination

csed.abroad.value: suspended while the taxpayer is outside the United States for a continuous period of at least 6 months, and not expiring before 6 months after return

csed.bankruptcy_tail.value: suspended while collection is barred by the bankruptcy case, plus 6 months

csed.custody_tail.value: suspended while the taxpayer's assets are in the control or custody of a court, plus 6 months

cdp.equivalent_hearing_window.value: one year — for a lien, commencing the day after the end of the five-business-day period following the NFTL filing; for a levy, commencing the day after the date of the CDP notice

cnc.hardship_codes.value: closing codes 24 through 32, available only for individual or joint IMF assessments, sole proprietorships, partnerships where a general partner is personally liable, and LLCs where an individual owner is the liable taxpayer

cnc.nftl_threshold.value: a Notice of Federal Tax Lien should generally be filed on an account reported CNC where the aggregate unpaid balance of assessments is $10,000 or more

refund.claim_period.value: 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever is later; 2 years from payment where no return was filed

refund.lookback.three_year.value: tax paid within the 3 years immediately preceding the claim, plus any period of extension of time for filing

refund.lookback.two_year.value: tax paid within the 2 years immediately preceding the claim

refund.baddebt_period.value: 7 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year the claim relates to

refund.nol_period.value: 3 years after the due date, including extensions, of the return for the loss year that produces the carryback, or the § 6511(c) period, whichever expires later

refund.ftc_period.value: 10 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year the foreign taxes were actually paid or accrued

refund.consent_tail.value: not before 6 months after the assessment period agreed under § 6501(c)(4) expires

refund.disability_suspension.value: suspended while an individual is financially disabled — unable to manage financial affairs through a medically determinable impairment expected to result in death or lasting at least 12 continuous months

amended.assessment_tail.value: where a signed document showing additional tax is received in the 60 days ending on the assessment deadline, the period for that additional amount runs 60 days from receipt

matherror.abatement_window.value: 60 days after the notice is sent, within which the taxpayer may request abatement and the Secretary must abate

deficiency.petition_period.value: 90 days after the notice of deficiency is mailed, or 150 days if addressed to a person outside the United States, not counting a Saturday, Sunday or District of Columbia legal holiday as the last day

cp2000.series.value: CP2000, CP2000A, CP2000B, CP2000C, CP2000D and CP2000E
cp2000.series.source: irs.gov, Understanding your CP2000 series notice, opened 2026-08-18

tfrp.amount.value: the total amount of the tax evaded, not collected, or not accounted for and paid over — the trust fund portion, without penalties or interest on the employer's account

tfrp.preliminary_notice.value: the preliminary notice must precede notice and demand by at least 60 days

tfrp.restriction_period.value: 60 days, or 75 days where the letter is addressed outside the United States, plus 5 additional days for receipt and processing of a timely mailed protest

tfrp.assessment_tail.value: not before the later of 90 days after the preliminary notice, or 30 days after a final administrative determination on a timely protest

tfrp.bond_stay.value: pay the minimum amount required to commence a court proceeding, file a refund claim, and furnish a bond, all within 30 days of notice and demand

passport.threshold.value: more than $66,000 of assessed, unpaid, legally enforceable federal tax liability including penalties and interest
passport.threshold.source: IRC § 7345(b)(1)(B), indexed under § 7345(f); Rev. Proc. 2025-32; irs.gov passport page opened 2026-08-18

passport.state_hold.value: 90 days from the date of the State Department's letter to arrange payment, pay in full, or resolve an erroneous certification
passport.state_hold.source: irs.gov, Revocation or denial of passport in cases of certain unpaid taxes, opened 2026-08-18

passport.reversal_timing.value: within 30 days of an installment agreement being entered into, an offer being accepted, or an innocent spouse election or request; and by the § 6325(a) lien release deadline where the debt is satisfied or becomes unenforceable

offset.priority.value: internal revenue tax first, then past-due child support, then debts owed to federal agencies, then past-due state income tax, then covered unemployment compensation debts

interest.suspension_36_months.value: 36 months from the later of the filing date or the unextended due date, for an individual who filed on time, after which interest and time-sensitive penalties are suspended until 21 days after the IRS gives notice

auditrecon.criteria.value: a return was filed; the assessment is unpaid or credits were reversed; the disputed adjustments are identified; and either new information not previously considered is supplied, or the IRS made a computational or processing error

auditrecon.collection_response.value: collection may be delayed on receipt, but may resume if the documentation does not support the position and the taxpayer does not answer a request for more information within 30 calendar days

extension.pay.return_period.value: a reasonable period not exceeding 6 months from the date fixed for payment, and longer where the taxpayer is abroad; 12 months for estate tax

extension.pay.deficiency_period.value: not exceeding 18 months from the date fixed for payment of the deficiency, and in exceptional cases a further period not exceeding 12 months

extension.pay.hardship.value: substantial financial loss, not mere inconvenience — a general statement of hardship will not do, and selling property at current market price where a market exists is not ordinarily hardship

extension.pay.support.value: Form 1127 with evidence of the hardship, a statement of assets and liabilities, and an itemised statement of all receipts and disbursements for each of the 3 months preceding the due date

extension.pay.bond.value: a bond not exceeding double the amount for which the extension is granted, where the Secretary requires security

decedent.prompt_assessment.value: 18 months from the date the written request is received, in place of the ordinary 3 years; available for any return of the decedent or the estate except the estate tax return

decedent.discharge_window.value: the IRS notifies the executor of the amount due within 9 months of the request; on payment, or if no notice issues in that period, the executor is discharged from personal liability

summons.appearance_days.value: not less than 10 days from the date of the summons

summons.thirdparty_notice.value: within 3 days of service, and no later than the 23rd day before the day fixed in the summons for examining the records

summons.quash_window.value: not later than the 20th day after notice is given, with a copy of the petition mailed to the person summoned and to the IRS within the same period

summons.thirdparty_contact_notice.value: at least 45 days before a period of not more than one year in which third-party contacts are intended

refund.direct_deposit_limit.value: 3 refunds electronically deposited into a single financial account or pre-paid debit card; the fourth and subsequent refunds convert to a paper check
refund.direct_deposit_limit.source: IRS, "Direct deposit limits," page last reviewed 30 September 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/refunds/direct-deposit-limits

ea.enrollment_fee.value: $140 to enroll initially, and $140 to renew
ea.enrollment_fee.source: 26 CFR §§ 300.5(b) and 300.6(b), applicable beginning 31 October 2022 (T.D. 9966) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/300.5 and /300.6

ea.ce.instruction_cap.value: 6 hours annually for enrolled agents and enrolled retirement plan agents, and 4 hours annually for registered tax return preparers, counting instruction and preparation together

ea.ce.contact_hour.value: 50 minutes of continuous participation; credit is granted only for a full contact hour or multiples of it, and a university semester hour equals 15 contact hours while a quarter hour equals 10

ea.ce.recordkeeping.value: 4 years following the date of renewal

shelter.material_advisor_threshold.value: $50,000 where substantially all the tax benefits go to natural persons, and $250,000 in any other case

shelter.6112_retention.value: 7 years, except as otherwise provided by regulation, with the list produced to the Secretary on written request

shelter.6707A_penalty.value: 75% of the decrease in tax shown on the return as a result of the transaction, capped at $200,000 for a listed transaction ($100,000 for a natural person) and $50,000 for any other reportable transaction ($10,000 for a natural person), and never less than $10,000 ($5,000 for a natural person)

shelter.6707_penalty.value: $50,000, or for a listed transaction the greater of $200,000 or 50% of the gross income derived from the aid, assistance or advice before the return is filed — 75% where the failure or act is intentional

caf.future_horizon.value: future tax periods may not exceed 3 years from 31 December of the year the IRS receives the power of attorney; periods beyond that are not recorded but the authorization stays valid and may be resubmitted
caf.future_horizon.source: Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 3, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i2848. Compare 26 CFR § 601.506(d)(3)(ii), which measures 3 years from the date of receipt.

caf.representative_limit.value: 3 representatives under a power of attorney, or 3 persons under a tax information authorization; where more are named only the first 3 are recorded, though all remain appointed

tia.nontax_purpose_window.value: 120 days from the taxpayer's signature date, for a Form 8821 authorizing disclosure for a purpose other than addressing or resolving a tax matter with the IRS — income verification for a lender, for example; the window does not apply where the purpose is assistance with an IRS tax matter
tia.nontax_purpose_window.source: Instructions for Form 8821 (When To File), page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8821

poa.notice_copy_limit.value: no more than 2 representatives on a Form 2848 — or designees on a Form 8821 — may be designated to receive copies of notices and communications for the same matters
poa.notice_copy_limit.source: Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 2, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i2848

poa.agent_signature_grounds.value: disease or injury; continuous absence from the United States, including Puerto Rico, for at least 60 days before the due date of the return; or specific permission requested of and granted by the IRS for other good cause
poa.agent_signature_grounds.source: Reg. § 1.6012-1(a)(5), quoted in the Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 5a — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.6012-1

disclosure.6103c_receipt_window.value: 120 days following the date the taxpayer signed and dated the request or consent — the IRS will not make the disclosure if it is received later

disclosure.7216_consent_duration.value: the period the consent document specifies; where it specifies none, 1 year from the date the taxpayer signed it

conference.submission_days.value: at least 5 business days before the conference for any written protest, brief or other statement the taxpayer or representative wishes considered; additional or supporting facts may follow within a reasonable time after it

interest.6404e_erroneous_refund_cap.value: the Secretary shall abate all interest on an erroneous refund until demand for repayment is made, unless the taxpayer or a related party caused it or the refund exceeds $50,000

interest.6404g_suspension.value: 36 months from the later of the filing date or the unextended due date, for a timely-filed individual subtitle A return; the suspension period runs from the day after that until 21 days after the IRS provides the notice

interest.6404h_tax_court_window.value: an action may be brought after the earlier of the final determination not to abate or 180 days from filing the claim, and no later than 180 days after the final determination is mailed

interest.rates_q3_2026.value: third quarter 2026: underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7%; non-corporate overpayment 7%; corporate overpayment 6%; GATT rate on a corporate overpayment exceeding $10,000, 4.5%; large corporate underpayment 9%; IRC § 6603 deposit (federal short-term) 4%
interest.rates_q3_2026.source: IRS, "Quarterly interest rates," 2026 rates by category, page last reviewed 2 July 2026 (3rd quarter rates per Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-22) — https://www.irs.gov/payments/quarterly-interest-rates

interest.notice_demand_grace.value: 21 calendar days after notice and demand, or 10 business days where the amount equals or exceeds $100,000 — interest is not imposed for the period after the notice on an amount paid within it

interest.rate_formula.value: the federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points for underpayments and for non-corporate overpayments; plus 2 points for a corporate overpayment, reduced to 0.5 point on the part exceeding $10,000; plus 5 points for a large corporate underpayment

interest.short_window_threshold.value: $100,000 — the statute says "equals or exceeds," so the short window applies at exactly that amount

interest.gatt_threshold.value: $10,000 — the part of a corporate overpayment above it takes the federal short-term rate plus 0.5 percentage point

abatement.843_claim_period.value: generally 3 years from the date the original return was filed or 2 years from the date the tax was paid, whichever is later
abatement.843_claim_period.source: Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024), Separate Form Required, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i843; IRC § 6511(a)

abatement.6404f_window.value: the request must be submitted within the period allowed for collection of the penalty or addition to tax, or the penalty must have been paid within the period allowed for claiming a credit or refund of it
abatement.6404f_window.source: Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024), When to file — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i843; IRC § 6404(f)

abatement.6676_penalty.value: 20% of the amount determined to be excessive, on an erroneous claim for refund or credit
abatement.6676_penalty.source: IRC § 6676(a), as described in the Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6676

exam.types.value: by mail (correspondence), or by in-person interview — at an IRS office (office audit) or at the taxpayer's home, place of business, or accountant's or representative's office (field audit)
exam.types.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.lookback.value: generally returns filed within the last 3 years; additional years may be added where a substantial error is identified, and the IRS usually does not go back more than 6 years — most audits are of returns filed within the last 2 years
exam.lookback.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.mail_extension.value: a one-time automatic 30-day extension is ordinarily granted for an audit conducted by mail; no additional time is available once a notice of deficiency has issued, and the 90-day Tax Court petition period cannot be extended
exam.mail_extension.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.record_retention.value: at least 3 years from the date the return was filed, for all records used to prepare it
exam.record_retention.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

privilege.7525_forums.value: any noncriminal tax matter before the IRS, and any noncriminal tax proceeding in Federal court brought by or against the United States

privilege.7525_shelter_exception.value: no privilege for any written communication between a federally authorized tax practitioner and any person (or that person's director, officer, employee, agent, representative, or capital- or profits-interest holder) in connection with the promotion of that person's direct or indirect participation in a tax shelter

privilege.tax_shelter_definition.value: a partnership or other entity, any investment plan or arrangement, or any other plan or arrangement, if a significant purpose of it is the avoidance or evasion of Federal income tax

exam.summons_appearance_days.value: the date fixed for appearance must be no less than 10 days from the date of the summons

exam.transfer_factors.value: 6 — the taxpayer's current residence; current principal place of business; where the books, records and source documents are maintained; where the Service can examine most efficiently; the Service resources available at the requested location; and other factors showing undue inconvenience

exam.transfer_sol_window.value: where a limitations period on assessment or collection will expire within 13 months of the request, the Service may condition an otherwise permissible transfer on a written extension of up to one year

exam.one_inspection.value: one inspection of a taxpayer's books of account per taxable year, unless the taxpayer requests otherwise or an authorized officer, after investigation, notifies the taxpayer in writing that an additional inspection is necessary

records.6001_standard.value: permanent books of account or records, including inventories, sufficient to establish the amount of gross income, deductions, credits, or other matters required to be shown on the return

records.retention_standard.value: kept at all times available for inspection by authorized internal revenue officers or employees, and retained so long as the contents may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law

records.274d_categories.value: 3 — traveling expenses under § 162 or § 212 (including meals and lodging while away from home), expenses for gifts, and listed property as defined in § 280F(d)(4)

records.274d_elements.value: 4 — the amount of the expense or other item; the time and place of the travel or the date and description of the gift; the business purpose; and the business relationship to the taxpayer of the person receiving the benefit

appeals.protest_threshold.value: $25,000 or less in proposed change to tax and penalties (or claimed refund) for each tax period permits a small case request; more than $25,000 for any tax period requires a formal written protest
appeals.protest_threshold.source: IRS Pub. 5 (Rev. 4-2021), "Small Case Request" and "Formal Written Protest"; IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025), "The Examination Process" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p5.pdf

appeals.protest_contents.value: a statement that you want to appeal, plus name, address and daytime telephone number; a list of all disputed issues, tax periods, proposed changes and reasons for disagreement; the facts supporting your position on each issue; the law or authority, if any, supporting it; a penalties of perjury statement; and your or your representative's signature under it

appeals.protest_window.value: the time limit specified in the letter — generally 30 days from the date of the letter
appeals.protest_window.source: IRS, "Preparing a request for appeals," page last reviewed 28 June 2026; IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025) — https://www.irs.gov/appeals/preparing-a-request-for-appeals

appeals.ased_remaining.value: generally 365 days must remain on the assessment statute expiration date when Appeals receives the case, and at least 270 days on the non-extendable ASED for estate tax cases
appeals.ased_remaining.source: IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025), "Consents to Extend the Assessment Statute Expiration Date" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p3498.pdf

exam.agreed_interest_grace.value: no further interest or penalty where a balance under $100,000 is paid within 21 calendar days of the bill, reduced to 10 business days where the amount is $100,000 or more

courts.forums.value: 3 — the United States Tax Court, the United States Court of Federal Claims, and the United States District Court for the judicial district where the taxpayer resides or has a principal place of business

courts.refund_suit_window.value: 2 years from the date of the notice of claim disallowance; Appeals' consideration of a disallowed claim does not extend it, though it may be extended by mutual agreement
courts.refund_suit_window.source: IRS Pub. 5 (Rev. 4-2021), "District Court and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p5.pdf

courts.refund_no_response.value: suit may be filed where no written response to a timely refund claim has been received within 6 months from the date the claim was filed

courts.frivolous_penalty.value: a penalty not in excess of $25,000, imposed by the Tax Court in its decision where proceedings were instituted or maintained primarily for delay, the taxpayer's position is frivolous or groundless, or the taxpayer unreasonably failed to pursue available administrative remedies

courts.small_tax_case.value: available where neither the deficiency in dispute nor any claimed overpayment exceeds $50,000 for any one taxable year (subtitle A), at the taxpayer's option concurred in by the Tax Court before hearing — the decision is not reviewable in any other court and is not treated as precedent

burden.default.value: on the petitioner, except as otherwise provided by statute or determined by the Court — and on the respondent as to any new matter, increases in deficiency, and affirmative defenses pleaded in the answer

burden.7491_conditions.value: 3 — the taxpayer has complied with the substantiation requirements of the Code; has maintained all required records and cooperated with reasonable requests for witnesses, information, documents, meetings and interviews; and, for a partnership, corporation or trust, meets the net worth and employee limits of IRC § 7430(c)(4)(A)(ii)

burden.7491_entity_limits.value: net worth not exceeding $7,000,000 and not more than 500 employees at the time the action was filed (individuals: net worth not exceeding $2,000,000)

burden.penalties.value: the Secretary carries the burden of production in any court proceeding as to the liability of any individual for any penalty, addition to tax, or additional amount

burden.fraud.value: on the respondent, carried by clear and convincing evidence

taxcourt.attorney_admission.value: an application, the Court's fee, and a current certificate from the Clerk of the appropriate court showing admission and good standing — executed within 90 calendar days preceding the filing of the application; no examination

taxcourt.nonattorney_admission.value: an application, the Court's fee, a written examination given by the Court held no less often than every 2 years and announced publicly at least 6 months in advance, and sponsorship by at least 2 persons already admitted (the Court may accept fewer in its discretion)

taxcourt.self_representation.value: an individual may represent himself or herself; an authorized officer may represent a corporation; an authorized individual may represent an unincorporated association; and a fiduciary may represent an estate or trust

practice.irs_scope.value: all matters connected with a presentation to the IRS or any of its officers or employees relating to a taxpayer's rights, privileges or liabilities — including preparing and filing documents, corresponding and communicating with the IRS, rendering written advice on any entity, transaction, plan or arrangement having a potential for tax avoidance or evasion, and representing a client at conferences, hearings and meetings

foia.exemptions.value: 9 — classified national defense and foreign policy documents; internal personnel rules and practices; information exempt under other laws; trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information; inter-agency or intra-agency memorandums or letters; personal privacy; law enforcement; financial institutions; and geological information
foia.exemptions.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(1)–(9), as described by IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.exclusions.value: 3 special protection provisions permitting especially sensitive law enforcement records to be treated as not subject to the FOIA, so that the IRS may respond that there are no responsive records — they apply only to information that is otherwise exempt and do not broaden the authority to withhold
foia.exclusions.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(c); IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.response_window.value: 20 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays, from receipt of the request, extendable by 10 additional days in unusual circumstances of which the requester must be notified
foia.response_window.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6); Reg. § 601.702(c)(11)(i)(A)(1)–(4); IRS FOIA guidelines, last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.appeal_window.value: an appeal must be postmarked within 90 days after the date of the denial letter (10 days where expedited processing was denied); the IRS must decide it within 20 days excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, extendable by 10
foia.appeal_window.source: 31 CFR Part 1 § 1.6, as described by IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.segregability.value: any reasonably segregable portion must be provided after the exempt portions are deleted, with the amount deleted and the exemption relied on indicated on the released record — and, where technically feasible, at the place on the record where the deletion was made — unless that indication would itself harm the protected interest

tas.reasons.value: 9, in 3 groups — financial hardship (reasons 1–4: hardship suffered or about to be suffered, immediate threat of negative action, major costs if relief is not granted, irreparable injury or long-term impact); IRS system issue (5–7: a delay of more than 30 days, no response or resolution by the date the IRS promised, a system or procedure that failed to operate as intended); and fair and equitable treatment (8–9: administration of the tax laws raising equity considerations or impairing taxpayer rights, and compelling public policy as determined by the National Taxpayer Advocate)
tas.reasons.source: Taxpayer Advocate Service, "Can TAS help me with my tax issue" — https://www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov/can-tas-help-me-with-my-tax-issue/

tas.significant_hardship.value: an immediate threat of adverse action; a delay of more than 30 days in resolving taxpayer account problems; the incurring of significant costs, including fees for professional representation, if relief is not granted; or irreparable injury to, or a long-term adverse impact on, the taxpayer if relief is not granted

tas.tao_terms.value: the Secretary may be required, within a specified time, to release levied property, or to cease, take, or refrain from any action under chapter 64 (collection), subchapter B of chapter 70 (bankruptcy and receiverships), chapter 78 (discovery of liability and enforcement), or any other provision specifically described in the order

tas.tao_rescission.value: only by the National Taxpayer Advocate, the Commissioner, or the Deputy Commissioner — and only if a written explanation of the reasons is provided to the National Taxpayer Advocate

tas.tao_suspension.value: any period of limitation on an action described in IRC § 7811(b) is suspended from the date of the taxpayer's application until the date of the National Taxpayer Advocate's decision, plus any period specified in the order

tas.nta_independence.value: the National Taxpayer Advocate may be appointed only if not an IRS officer or employee during the 2-year period ending with the appointment, and must agree not to accept IRS employment for at least 5 years after leaving — service in the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate is disregarded

evasion.7201.value: a felony — willfully attempting in any manner to evade or defeat any tax or its payment; fine of not more than $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution

evasion.7203.value: a misdemeanor — willful failure to pay estimated tax or tax, file a return, keep records, or supply information when required; fine of not more than $25,000 ($100,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 1 year, or both — raised to a felony with 5 years for a willful violation of § 6050I

evasion.7206.value: a felony — willfully signing a return or document verified under penalties of perjury that the signer does not believe true and correct as to every material matter, or willfully aiding or assisting in preparing a materially false or fraudulent document; fine of not more than $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 3 years, or both

evasion.title18_fines.value: the fine is the greatest of the amount in the offense statute or, for a felony, $250,000 for an individual and $500,000 for an organization — so the $100,000 stated in IRC §§ 7201 and 7206 is superseded upward for individuals unless the offense statute exempts itself by specific reference

evasion.civil_fraud.value: 75 percent of the portion of the underpayment attributable to fraud; where the Secretary establishes that any portion is attributable to fraud the entire underpayment is so treated, except any portion the taxpayer shows by a preponderance of the evidence is not

idtheft.ippin_validity.value: a six-digit number valid for one calendar year, with a new one generated each year; it is used only on Forms 1040, 1040-NR, 1040-PR, 1040-SR and 1040-SS, must be used on any federal return filed during the year including prior-year returns, and is generally viewable in the online account from mid-January through mid-November
idtheft.ippin_validity.source: IRS, Get an identity protection PIN (page last reviewed or updated 4 August 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_delivery.value: a confirmed victim enrolled by the IRS receives a CP01A Notice with the new IP PIN each year; a taxpayer who opted in and obtained the IP PIN online must retrieve it online each year, because no CP01A is mailed
idtheft.ippin_delivery.source: IRS, "Get an identity protection PIN," page last reviewed 4 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_routes.value: 3 — through the IRS online account (fastest; required for anyone aged 18 or over who can validate identity online); by Form 15227 where adjusted gross income on the last filed return is below $84,000, or $168,000 for married filing jointly, with identity validated by telephone and the IP PIN mailed in about four to six weeks; or by an in-person appointment at a Taxpayer Assistance Center with two forms of identification, with the IP PIN mailed in about three weeks
idtheft.ippin_routes.source: IRS, "Get an identity protection PIN," page last reviewed 4 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.steps.value: stop interacting with the thief; update the Online Account password; follow the instructions in the IRS letter or notice; report the theft and follow the recovery steps at IdentityTheft.gov; get an IP PIN; keep records of letters, calls and emails; file returns and pay tax as usual; and check with the state tax agency
idtheft.steps.source: IRS, "Identity theft guide for individuals," page last reviewed 4 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/taxpayer-guide-to-identity-theft

idtheft.dependent_efile.value: beginning with 2024 tax returns the IRS accepts e-filed Forms 1040, 1040-NR and 1040-SS even where a dependent has already been claimed on another return, provided the primary taxpayer on the second return includes a valid IP PIN — the dependent needs no IP PIN unless one was previously issued
idtheft.dependent_efile.source: IRS, "Identity theft guide for individuals," page last reviewed 4 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/taxpayer-guide-to-identity-theft

disclosure.8275_scope.value: discloses items or positions not otherwise adequately disclosed, except those taken contrary to a regulation; it avoids the disregard-of-rules and substantial-understatement portions of the accuracy-related penalty for non-tax-shelter items where the position has a reasonable basis, and may be used for the economic substance disclosure and the preparer penalties
disclosure.8275_scope.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Purpose of Form" — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.8275r_scope.value: discloses positions taken contrary to Treasury regulations; it avoids the disregard-of-regulations and substantial-understatement portions for non-tax-shelter items where the position has a reasonable basis — and cannot avoid the disregard of rules other than regulations, which is Form 8275's territory
disclosure.8275r_scope.source: Instructions for Form 8275-R (Rev. 11/2024), "Purpose of Form" — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275r

disclosure.not_curable.value: negligence; substantial understatement on a tax shelter item; substantial or gross valuation misstatements under chapter 1, including non-arm's-length prices; substantial overstatement of pension liabilities; substantial estate or gift tax valuation understatements; tax benefits from a transaction lacking economic substance under § 7701(o); undisclosed foreign financial asset understatements; inconsistent estate basis; overstatement of the § 170(p) deduction; and disallowance under § 170(h)(7)
disclosure.not_curable.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024) and Form 8275-R (Rev. 11/2024) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.adequate_standard.value: the position must be adequately disclosed and have at least a reasonable basis; to avoid the disregard-of-regulations portion it must also represent a good-faith challenge to the validity of the regulation — and disclosure cannot cure a failure to keep proper books and records or to substantiate items
disclosure.adequate_standard.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Adequate disclosure"; Reg. § 1.6662-3(c)(1) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.reasonable_basis.value: a relatively high standard of tax reporting, significantly higher than not frivolous or not patently improper, and not satisfied by a position that is merely arguable; a position reasonably based on an authority in Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii) generally satisfies it even if it does not meet the substantial authority standard
disclosure.reasonable_basis.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Reasonable basis"; Reg. §§ 1.6662-4(d), 1.6662-3(b)(3) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

summons.7609_notice.value: notice to the identified person within 3 days of service, and no later than the 23rd day before the day fixed in the summons for examination of the records — accompanied by a copy of the summons served and an explanation of the right to bring a proceeding to quash

summons.7609_quash.value: a proceeding to quash must be begun not later than the 20th day after notice is given, and within the same 20 days a copy of the petition must be mailed by registered or certified mail to the person summoned and to the office the Secretary directs in the notice

summons.7609_exceptions.value: 5 — a summons served on the person whose liability is in issue or their officer or employee; one issued to determine whether records of an identified person's business transactions have been made or kept; one issued solely to identify a person with a numbered account; one issued in aid of collection of an assessment or judgment against that person, or of a transferee's or fiduciary's liability; and one issued by an IRS criminal investigator and served on someone who is not a third-party recordkeeper

summons.7609_suspension.value: the § 6501 assessment and § 6531 criminal periods are suspended while a proceeding brought by the taxpayer under § 7609(b) and any appeals are pending; and, for anyone else, from 6 months after service of the summons until the summoned party's response is finally resolved

summons.john_doe.value: 3 findings a court must make before a John Doe summons may be served — that it relates to the investigation of a particular person or ascertainable group or class; that there is a reasonable basis for believing they may have failed to comply with an internal revenue law; and that the information is not readily available from other sources — and the information sought must be narrowly tailored to that failure

summons.service.value: an attested copy delivered in hand to the person to whom it is directed, or left at that person's last and usual place of abode — with the additional option, for a third-party recordkeeper, of certified or registered mail to the last known address

summons.recordkeepers.value: banks, savings institutions and credit unions; consumer reporting agencies; persons extending credit through credit cards or similar devices; brokers; attorneys; accountants; barter exchanges; regulated investment companies and their agents; enrolled agents; and owners or developers of computer software source code

timely.mailing_rule.value: the date of the United States postmark on the cover is deemed the date of delivery or payment, provided the postmark date falls within the prescribed period (including any extension) and the item was deposited within that time in the US mail, postage prepaid, properly addressed

timely.mailing_exceptions.value: 3 — filings in or payments to any court other than the Tax Court; currency or other medium of payment unless actually received and accounted for; and items required by law or regulation to be delivered by a method other than mailing

timely.registered_mail.value: registration is prima facie evidence of delivery and the date of registration is deemed the postmark date; the Secretary is authorised to extend both by regulation to certified mail and electronic filing

timely.pds.value: 3 designated carriers — DHL Express, FedEx and UPS — but only for the specific services the IRS lists; a service not on the list does not get the timely-mailing rule
timely.pds.source: IRC § 7502(f) and IRS, "Private delivery services (PDS)," page last reviewed 28 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/filing/private-delivery-services-pds

timely.weekend_holiday.value: where the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, performance on the next succeeding day that is none of those is timely — the last day is determined including any authorized extension, and "legal holiday" means a legal holiday in the District of Columbia

timely.disaster_discretionary.value: the Secretary may specify a period of up to 1 year to be disregarded for a taxpayer affected by a federally declared disaster, a significant fire, or a terroristic or military action — and, on the written request of a Governor, for a qualified State declared disaster

timely.disaster_mandatory.value: 120 days, running from the earliest incident date in the declaration to 120 days after the later of that date or the date the declaration was issued, disregarded automatically for a qualified taxpayer — in addition to or concurrent with any period the Secretary specifies
timely.disaster_mandatory.source: IRC § 7508A(e), as amended by Pub. L. 119-29 § 2 (2025), which substituted 120 days for 60 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/7508A

authority.list.value: applicable provisions of the Code and other statutes; proposed, temporary and final regulations construing them; revenue rulings and revenue procedures; tax treaties and regulations thereunder and official explanations of them; court cases; congressional intent in committee reports, conference-report joint explanatory statements and pre-enactment floor statements by a bill's managers; Joint Committee on Taxation General Explanations (the Blue Book); private letter rulings and technical advice memoranda issued after 31 October 1976; actions on decisions and general counsel memoranda issued after 12 March 1981, and GCMs in pre-1955 Cumulative Bulletin volumes; IRS information or press releases; and notices, announcements and other administrative pronouncements published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin

authority.not_authority.value: conclusions reached in treatises, legal periodicals, legal opinions, or opinions rendered by tax professionals — though the authorities underlying those opinions may themselves give rise to substantial authority

authority.substantial_standard.value: an objective standard, less stringent than more likely than not (a greater than 50-percent likelihood) but more stringent than reasonable basis; met only where the weight of supporting authorities is substantial in relation to the weight of contrary authorities, all relevant authorities being taken into account

authority.ceases.value: an authority stops being one to the extent it is overruled or modified, implicitly or explicitly, by a body with power to do so — but a Tax Court opinion is not treated as overruled by a court of appeals to which the taxpayer has no right of appeal unless the Tax Court adopts that holding, and a private letter ruling is not authority if revoked or inconsistent with a later proposed regulation, revenue ruling or IRB pronouncement

authority.written_determination.value: a ruling, determination letter, technical advice memorandum, or Chief Counsel advice; unless the Secretary provides otherwise by regulation it may not be used or cited as precedent — yet it does give the taxpayer it was issued to substantial authority for that treatment

guidance.revenue_ruling.value: an official interpretation by the Service published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, issued only by the National Office, for the information and guidance of taxpayers, IRS officials and others concerned

guidance.revenue_procedure.value: a statement of procedure affecting the rights or duties of taxpayers or other members of the public under the Code and related statutes, or information that should be a matter of public knowledge although not necessarily affecting those rights and duties

guidance.ruling_weight.value: revenue rulings do not have the force and effect of Treasury regulations, but are published to provide precedents to be used in disposing of other cases and may be cited and relied on for that purpose — while no unpublished ruling or decision may be relied on, used or cited as a precedent by any IRS officer or employee

guidance.ruling_reliance.value: taxpayers generally may rely on published revenue rulings and need not request a specific ruling applying their principles — but each ruling states the Service's conclusion on the entire state of facts involved, so the same conclusion should not be reached in another case unless the facts and circumstances are substantially the same, and the effect of subsequent legislation, regulations, court decisions and revenue rulings must be considered

guidance.retroactivity.value: revenue rulings apply retroactively unless the ruling states, under IRC § 7805(b), the extent to which it is to apply without retroactive effect — an affirmative act; where a ruling revokes or modifies an earlier published one, § 7805(b) is ordinarily invoked so the new ruling is not applied retroactively to a taxpayer's detriment

guidance.reg_retroactivity.value: no temporary, proposed or final regulation applies to a taxable period ending before the earliest of the date it is filed with the Federal Register, the date a related proposed or temporary regulation was so filed, or the date a notice substantially describing its expected contents was issued — with exceptions for regulations issued within 18 months of the statute, to prevent abuse, to correct a procedural defect, for internal Treasury policies, on congressional authorization, and by taxpayer election

plr.definition.value: a written statement issued to a taxpayer or their authorized representative by the National Office, which interprets and applies the tax laws to a specific set of facts; rulings are issued only by the National Office

plr.determination_letter.value: a written statement issued in response to a written inquiry, applying to the particular facts the principles and precedents previously announced by the National Office — issued only where the determination can be made on clearly established rules in a statute, Treasury decision, regulation, or a ruling, opinion or court decision published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, and not where the question is novel

plr.information_letter.value: a statement that does no more than call attention to a well-established interpretation or principle of tax law, without applying it to a specific set of facts — issued where the request seeks general information or does not meet all the requirements for a ruling

plr.user_fees.value: user fees are required for requests for ruling letters, opinion letters and determination letters; they vary by category, are set after taking account of the average time for and difficulty of the category, and are payable in advance — with exemptions and reduced fees as the Secretary determines appropriate

reg.forms.value: the most important internal revenue rules are issued as regulations and Treasury decisions, prescribed by the Commissioner and approved by the Secretary or delegate; they are prepared in the Office of the Chief Counsel, approved by the Commissioner, then forwarded to the Secretary or delegate for final approval

reg.notice_and_comment.value: where 5 U.S.C. § 553 requires it, general notice of proposed rules is published in the Federal Register, stating the time, place and nature of the public rulemaking proceedings, the authority under which the rule is proposed, and either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved

reg.temporary.value: any temporary regulation must also be issued as a proposed regulation, and expires within 3 years after the date of issuance

reg.authority.value: except where the authority is expressly given to someone outside the Treasury Department, the Secretary prescribes all needful rules and regulations for the enforcement of the title, including those needed by reason of any alteration of law

reg.small_business_review.value: after publication of a proposed or temporary regulation the Secretary submits it to the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration, who has 4 weeks to comment on its impact on small business; those comments must be considered before a superseding final regulation is prescribed

irm.definition.value: the single official source of instructions to staff — based on and including the policies, delegated authorities, procedures, instructions and guidelines relating to the organization, functions, administration and operations of the IRS

irm.parts.value: the parts most used in representation are 4 Examining Process, 5 Collecting Process, 8 Appeals, 13 Taxpayer Advocate Service, 20 Penalty and Interest, 21 Customer Account Services and 25 Special Topics; parts 30 to 39 are the Chief Counsel Directives Manual
irm.parts.source: IRS, "Internal Revenue Manual" table of contents — https://www.irs.gov/irm

irm.efoia.value: 3 conditions — the guidance must be procedural and communicate directions, guidelines or standards to employees in performing their duties; affect how a member of the public files, pays, complies or interacts with the IRS; and not be exempt under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)
irm.efoia.source: IRM 1.11.1.3.1.2 (24 April 2014), "E-FOIA Criteria for Instructions to Staff" — https://www.irs.gov/irm/part1/irm_01-011-001

irm.ouo.value: instructions to staff affecting the public must be made public unless exempt under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b); generally only § 552(b)(7)(E) applies — content whose disclosure could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of the law, designated official use only and redacted before posting, with the remaining content accessible
irm.ouo.source: IRM 1.11.1.3.1.3 (7 October 2022), "Disclosure Exemptions for Instructions to Staff" — https://www.irs.gov/irm/part1/irm_01-011-001

irm.interim_guidance.value: used to convey new, changed, pilot or temporary procedure, or a deviation from procedure, where there is insufficient time to update and publish the IRM — so an IRM section can be current on its face and superseded by an interim guidance memorandum

caselaw.weight.value: a Supreme Court decision becomes the law of the land, takes precedence over lower courts, must be followed by the IRS, and for examiners has the same weight as the Code; decisions of the Tax Court, District Courts and the Court of Federal Claims bind the IRS only for the particular taxpayer and the years litigated, and an adverse lower-court decision does not require the IRS to alter its position for other taxpayers

caselaw.taxcourt_opinions.value: 3 — regular opinions, which involve more than mere factual determinations or applications of well-established principles and generally decide new points of law that set precedents; memorandum decisions, which primarily involve factual determinations and the application of well-established rules; and small tax case decisions, which are final, may not be appealed by either party, and have no precedential value

caselaw.aod.value: issued at the IRS's discretion only on unappealed issues decided adverse to the government; it is not an affirmative statement of IRS position, is not intended as public guidance, and may not be cited as precedent — relied on within the IRS only as the conclusion applying the law to the facts of that case at that time

caselaw.acquiescence.value: 3 recommendations — acquiescence, meaning the IRS accepts the holding and will follow it on the same controlling facts, indicating neither approval nor disapproval of the court's reasons; acquiescence in result only, same acceptance but signalling disagreement or concern with some or all of those reasons; and nonacquiescence, meaning the IRS does not agree and generally will not follow the decision for other taxpayers, though it recognises the precedential impact within the deciding circuit

pubs.status.value: IRS publications explain the law in plain language, highlight changes, give examples of IRS positions and include worksheets — but they are nonbinding on the IRS, do not necessarily cover all positions for an issue, and "should not be cited to sustain a position"

pubs.informal_guidance.value: forms, instructions, publications and IRS.gov webpages — they do not apply the law to taxpayer-specific facts, may not reflect special rules or exceptions, have not been published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, and "will not be relied on, used, or cited as precedents by Service personnel in the disposition of cases"
pubs.informal_guidance.source: IRS, "General overview of taxpayer reliance on guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin and FAQs," page last reviewed 5 December 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.law_controls.value: if information in informal guidance or an FAQ turns out to be an inaccurate statement of the law as applied to a particular taxpayer's case, the law controls the taxpayer's tax liability — only guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin has precedential value
pubs.law_controls.source: IRS, "General overview of taxpayer reliance on guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin and FAQs," page last reviewed 5 December 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.reliance_penalty.value: a taxpayer who shows reliance in good faith that was reasonable on all the facts and circumstances will not be subject to a penalty carrying a reasonable cause standard — including a negligence or other accuracy-related penalty — to the extent the reliance results in an underpayment
pubs.reliance_penalty.source: IRS reliance page (last reviewed 5 December 2025), citing Reg. § 1.6664-4(b) — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.factsheet_faq.value: FAQs published in a Fact Sheet linked to an IRS news release are considered authority for the substantial authority exception to accuracy-related penalties; FAQs not published in the Bulletin are not
pubs.factsheet_faq.source: IRS reliance page (last reviewed 5 December 2025), citing Reg. § 1.6662-4(d) — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

treaty.no_preference.value: in determining the relationship between a treaty provision and any United States revenue law, neither the treaty nor the law has preferential status by reason of being a treaty or a law — so the later in time generally prevails

treaty.due_regard.value: the provisions of the title are applied to any taxpayer with due regard to any treaty obligation of the United States that applies to that taxpayer

treaty.disclosure.value: a taxpayer taking the position that a treaty overrules or otherwise modifies an internal revenue law must disclose that position on the return, or on a statement attached to it, or in the form the Secretary prescribes where no return is required — the Secretary may waive the requirement for classes of cases

treaty.disclosure_penalty.value: $1,000 per failure, or $10,000 in the case of a C corporation, waivable in whole or part on a showing of reasonable cause and good faith, and in addition to any other penalty imposed by law

treaty.saving_clause.value: most income tax treaties contain a saving clause, which prevents a citizen or resident of the United States from using the treaty to avoid taxation of U.S. source income
treaty.saving_clause.source: IRS, "United States income tax treaties — A to Z," page last reviewed 3 January 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/international-businesses/united-states-income-tax-treaties-a-to-z

conflict.definition.value: 2 — the representation of one client will be directly adverse to another client, or there is a significant risk that representation of one or more clients will be materially limited by the practitioner's responsibilities to another client, a former client or a third person, or by a personal interest of the practitioner

conflict.waiver.value: 3 conditions — the practitioner reasonably believes they can provide competent and diligent representation to each affected client; the representation is not prohibited by law; and each affected client waives the conflict and gives informed consent, confirmed in writing, at the time the conflict is known, with the written confirmation made within a reasonable period and in no event later than 30 days

conflict.retention.value: copies of the written consents must be retained for at least 36 months from the date the representation of the affected clients concluded, and must be provided to any IRS officer or employee on request

competence.standard.value: the appropriate level of knowledge, skill, thoroughness and preparation necessary for the matter for which the practitioner is engaged — attainable through various methods, such as consulting with experts in the relevant area or studying the relevant law

diligence.reliance.value: a practitioner is presumed to have exercised due diligence where they rely on the work product of another person and used reasonable care in engaging, supervising, training and evaluating that person, taking proper account of the nature of the relationship — except as modified by §§ 10.34 and 10.37

diligence.scope.value: 3 — in preparing or assisting in the preparation of, approving, and filing returns, documents, affidavits and other papers relating to IRS matters; in determining the correctness of oral or written representations made to the Treasury Department; and in determining the correctness of oral or written representations made to clients on any matter administered by the IRS

competence.firm_procedures.value: an individual with, or sharing, principal authority and responsibility for overseeing a firm's practice must take reasonable steps to ensure the firm has adequate procedures for all members, associates and employees to comply with subparts A, B and C — and where the firm identifies nobody, the IRS may identify who is responsible

competence.firm_discipline.value: discipline requires willfulness, recklessness or gross incompetence in failing to ensure adequate procedures exist, or that they are followed, or in failing to take prompt corrective action — together with a pattern or practice of non-compliance by one or more members, associates or employees

competence.prompt_disposition.value: a practitioner may not unreasonably delay the prompt disposition of any matter before the Internal Revenue Service

criminal.referral_bar.value: no summons may be issued, and no § 7604 enforcement action begun, with respect to any person while a Justice Department referral is in effect for that person — each taxable period and each tax imposed by a separate chapter being treated separately

criminal.referral_trigger.value: a referral is in effect once the Secretary has recommended to the Attorney General a grand jury investigation of, or the criminal prosecution of, the person for an offence connected with the administration or enforcement of the internal revenue laws, or once a request is made under § 6103(h)(3)(B) for disclosure of that person's return or return information

criminal.financial_status.value: the Secretary shall not use financial status or economic reality examination techniques to determine the existence of unreported income unless there is a reasonable indication that unreported income is likely

criminal.omission_duty.value: a practitioner who knows a client has not complied with the revenue laws, or has made an error in or omission from any return, document, affidavit or other paper submitted or executed under them, must advise the client promptly of that fact and of the consequences under the Code and regulations

transcript.types.value: six through the Transcript Delivery System — tax return, tax account, record of account, wage and income (individual only), verification of non-filing letter (individual only), and the business entity transcripts (business only)

transcript.availability.value: tax return transcript and record of account, the current and 3 prior tax years; tax account transcript, the current and 9 prior years through the Individual Online Account or the current and 3 prior by mail or phone; wage and income transcript, the current and 9 prior years; verification of non-filing, after 15 June for the current year or any time for the prior 3 — older years by Form 4506-T
transcript.availability.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.wage_limit.value: a wage and income transcript is limited to approximately 85 income documents; beyond that it will not generate through the Individual Online Account and Form 4506-T must be submitted — and current processing year information is generally available in the first week of February
transcript.wage_limit.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.tds_access.value: EROs and Circular 230 practitioners may request account transcripts, wage and income documents, tax return transcripts, record of account and verification of non-filing letters through the Transcript Delivery System — a properly executed Form 2848 or Form 8821 must be on file
transcript.tds_access.source: IRS, "Transcript Delivery System (TDS)," page last reviewed 10 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/transcript-delivery-system-tds

transcript.not_a_copy.value: a transcript is not a photocopy of the return; a copy of the original return is obtained on Form 4506, which carries a processing time and a fee
transcript.not_a_copy.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

advice.written_requirements.value: 6 — base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions including as to future events; reasonably consider all relevant facts and circumstances the practitioner knows or reasonably should know; use reasonable efforts to identify and ascertain the facts relevant to each Federal tax matter; not rely on representations, statements, findings or agreements of the taxpayer or anyone else where reliance would be unreasonable; relate applicable law and authorities to facts; and not take into account the possibility that a return will not be audited or a matter not raised on audit

advice.unreasonable_reliance.value: reliance on representations, statements, findings or agreements is unreasonable if the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that one or more of the representations, or assumptions on which any representation is based, are incorrect, incomplete or inconsistent

advice.client_information.value: a practitioner generally may rely in good faith without verification on information furnished by the client — but may not ignore the implications of information furnished to or actually known by them, and must make reasonable inquiries if the information appears incorrect, inconsistent with an important fact or another factual assumption, or incomplete

advice.penalty_warning.value: a practitioner must inform the client of any penalties reasonably likely to apply to a position on a return where the practitioner advised on it or prepared or signed the return, and to any document, affidavit or other paper submitted to the IRS — and must inform the client of any opportunity to avoid them by disclosure and of the requirements for adequate disclosure, whether or not the practitioner is themselves exposed

advice.reliance_on_others.value: a practitioner may rely on another person's advice only if it was reasonable and the reliance is in good faith on all the facts and circumstances — and reliance is not reasonable where the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the opinion should not be relied on, that the person is not competent or lacks the necessary qualifications, or that the person has a conflict of interest in violation of Circular 230

residency.closer_connection.value: presence on fewer than 183 days in the current year, together with a tax home in and a closer connection to a foreign country

carryover.capital_loss_period.value: indefinite, with the short-term and long-term components carried forward separately and retaining their character

carryover.charitable_period.value: the 5 succeeding taxable years, in order of time, subject in each year to the same percentage limitation

carryover.passive.value: carried to the next taxable year as a deduction or credit allocable to the same activity, with no time limit

carryover.amt_credit.value: the adjusted net minimum tax imposed for all prior taxable years beginning after 1986, less amounts already allowed as a credit

dependency.qr_gross_income.value: $5,300 — the exemption amount referred to in IRC § 152(d)(1)(B) for taxable years beginning in 2026

dependency.qc_tests.value: 5 — relationship, the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than half the year, the age requirement, that the individual has not provided over half of their own support, and that the individual has not filed a joint return other than to claim a refund

dependency.qc_age.value: under 19 at the close of the calendar year, or under 24 if a student, and in either case younger than the taxpayer; any age if permanently and totally disabled at any time during the year

dependency.qr_tests.value: 4 — the relationship or member-of-household test, gross income below the exemption amount, support of over one-half provided by the taxpayer, and that the individual is not a qualifying child of the taxpayer or of any other taxpayer

dependency.tiebreak.value: a parent over a non-parent; between parents not filing jointly, the one with whom the child resided longest, then the higher adjusted gross income; where no parent claims, another taxpayer only if their adjusted gross income exceeds the highest of any parent's

dependency.multiple_support.value: the taxpayer must contribute over 10 percent of support, no one person may contribute over half, over half must come from persons who would each otherwise qualify, and every other such person contributing over 10 percent must file a written declaration

exemption.tin_required.value: no exemption is allowed with respect to an individual unless that individual's TIN is included on the return claiming it

kiddie.threshold.value: $2,700 of unearned income before any is taxed at the parent's rate — twice the § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) amount, being that amount plus the greater of it or directly connected itemized deductions

kiddie.election_conditions.value: 4 — the child's gross income is only from interest and dividends, it falls within the stated range, no estimated tax payments or backup withholding stand in the child's name and TIN, and the parent elects

aca.enhanced_percentages_expired.value: the temporary premium percentages likewise applied only to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2020 and before 1 January 2026
