aca.aptc_repayment.source: Pub. L. 119-21 § 71305, as described in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.04 — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

aca.ale_threshold.value: an employer who employed an average of at least 50 full-time employees on business days during the preceding calendar year

fbar.threshold.value: an aggregate value of the foreign financial accounts exceeding $10,000 at any time during the calendar year reported
fbar.threshold.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

fbar.due_date.value: April 15 following the calendar year reported, with an automatic extension to October 15 that need not be requested
fbar.due_date.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

f8938.threshold_single.value: exceeding $50,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $75,000 at any time during the year

f8938.threshold_joint.value: exceeding $100,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $150,000 at any time during the year

f8938.threshold_abroad.value: exceeding $200,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $300,000 at any time during the year, for a specified individual who is a qualified individual under IRC § 911(d)(1)

f8938.threshold_joint_abroad.value: exceeding $400,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $600,000 at any time during the year

f8938.penalty.value: $10,000, plus $10,000 for each 30-day period or fraction of one during which the failure continues more than 90 days after the Secretary mails notice, to a maximum continuation penalty of $50,000

fbar.exclusions.value: 7 categories the IRS lists as not reportable — correspondent or Nostro accounts, accounts owned by a governmental entity, accounts owned by an international financial institution, accounts maintained on a U.S. military banking facility, accounts held in an IRA of which the person is owner or beneficiary, accounts held in a retirement plan of which the person is participant or beneficiary, and accounts held in a trust of which the person is a beneficiary where a U.S. person files an FBAR reporting them
fbar.exclusions.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

duedate.nonresident_alien.value: the 15th day of June following the close of the calendar year, or the 15th day of the sixth month following a fiscal year, for a nonresident alien individual whose wages are not subject to chapter 24 withholding

combat.disregarded_period.value: the period of service in the combat zone or contingency operation, plus any period of continuous qualified hospitalization attributable to an injury received there, plus the next 180 days

offset.support_priority.value: past-due support certified by a State is applied first, before any other reduction allowed by law

itemized.salt_cap.value: $40,400 for taxable years beginning in calendar year 2026 (half that on a married filing separate return), rising 1 percent a year through 2029 and reverting to $10,000 for years beginning after 2029

itemized.salt_threshold.value: $505,000 of modified adjusted gross income for 2026 (half that on a married filing separate return), above which the cap falls by 30 cents on the dollar but never below $10,000

itemized.mortgage_cap.value: $750,000 of acquisition indebtedness ($375,000 on a married filing separate return), with debt incurred on or before 15 December 2017 still measured against the older $1,000,000 limit

itemized.medical_floor.value: expenses above 7.5 percent of adjusted gross income

itemized.charitable_floor.value: only contributions above 0.5 percent of the taxpayer's contribution base, applied for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025

itemized.haircut.value: itemized deductions reduced by 2/37 of the lesser of those deductions or the taxable income above the point where the 37 percent bracket begins, first applying to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025

deduction.charitable_nonitemizer.value: up to $1,000 ($2,000 on a joint return) of cash contributions to a § 170(b)(1)(A) organization other than a supporting organization or donor advised fund

deduction.tips_cap.value: $25,000 of qualified tips, reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000 ($300,000 on a joint return)

deduction.overtime_cap.value: $12,500 of qualified overtime compensation ($25,000 on a joint return), reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000 ($300,000 on a joint return)

deduction.vehicle_interest_cap.value: $10,000 of interest on a first-lien loan for a personal-use passenger vehicle bought after 31 December 2024, reduced by $200 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $100,000 ($200,000 on a joint return), for years before 2029

transcript.return_years.value: the current and three prior tax years
transcript.return_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.account_years.value: the current and nine prior tax years through Individual Online Account, but only the current and three prior years by mail or telephone; older years need Form 4506-T
transcript.account_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.wage_years.value: the current and nine prior tax years, with the current processing year generally available in the first week of February
transcript.wage_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.wage_doc_limit.value: approximately 85 income documents, above which the transcript will not generate through Individual Online Account and Form 4506-T is required
transcript.wage_doc_limit.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.nonfiling_window.value: after 15 June for the current tax year, or at any time for the prior three tax years; Form 4506-T for older years
transcript.nonfiling_window.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.schedule_c_limit.value: three, because Submission Processing transcribes only three; data for any further Schedule C is consolidated into the totals

income.61_items.value: fourteen, from compensation for services through income from an interest in an estate or trust — a list expressly not exhaustive, and one item shorter since alimony was struck for post-2018 instruments

info.1099k_threshold.value: more than $20,000 in aggregate payments and more than 200 transactions, both required, restored retroactively as if the $600 threshold had never been enacted

ss.base_amount.value: $25,000, or $32,000 on a joint return, and zero for a married taxpayer who does not file jointly and did not live apart from their spouse for the whole year — none of which is indexed for inflation

ss.adjusted_base_amount.value: $34,000, or $44,000 on a joint return, and zero in the same married-filing-separately case; also unindexed

ss.inclusion_ceiling.value: at most 85 percent of benefits are included in gross income; the first tier includes the lesser of half the benefits or half the excess over the base amount

feie.housing.value: housing expenses above 16 percent of the exclusion amount, capped at 30 percent of it, both computed on a daily basis over the qualifying period

ira.deduction_limit.value: $7,500, plus a further $1,100 for an individual who has attained age 50 before the close of the taxable year

ira.active_participant_phaseout.value: $81,000 to $91,000 for a single active participant; $129,000 to $149,000 on a joint return where the contributing spouse is an active participant; $242,000 to $252,000 where only the other spouse is; and an unindexed $0 to $10,000 for a married active participant filing separately

hsa.contribution_limit.value: $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage, plus an unindexed $1,000 for an individual who has attained age 55 before the close of the taxable year

hsa.hdhp.value: an annual deductible of at least $1,700 for self-only or $3,400 for family coverage, with annual out-of-pocket expenses not exceeding $8,500 or $17,000 respectively

studentloan.deduction.value: $2,500, phasing out between $85,000 and $100,000 of modified adjusted gross income, or between $175,000 and $205,000 on a joint return

educator.deduction.value: $350 of the expenses of an eligible educator — a kindergarten through grade 12 teacher, instructor, counselor, principal or aide for at least 900 hours in a school year

dependentcare.exclusion.value: $7,500, or $3,750 on a separate return by a married individual, raised from $5,000 and $2,500 for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
dependentcare.exclusion.source: IRC § 129(a)(2)(A) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70404(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/129

edassist.exclusion.value: $5,250, unchanged for 2026 and first indexed for taxable years beginning after 2026
edassist.exclusion.source: IRC § 127(a)(2), (d)(1) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70412(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/127

ctc.amount.value: $2,200 per qualifying child, phasing out above a threshold of $400,000 on a joint return and $200,000 in any other case
ctc.amount.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05(1); IRC § 24(h)(2), (h)(3) as made permanent by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24

ctc.refundable_portion.value: $1,700 per qualifying child, indexed from the $1,400 base in IRC § 24(h)(5), with the refundable amount computed from earned income above $2,500

ctc.other_dependents.value: $500 for each dependent who is not a qualifying child, non-refundable and not indexed

dcc.applicable_percentage.value: 50 percent, reduced by one point for each $2,000 of adjusted gross income above $15,000 but not below 35 percent, then further reduced by one point for each $2,000 ($4,000 joint) above $75,000 ($150,000 joint) but not below 20 percent
dcc.applicable_percentage.source: IRC § 21(a)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

dcc.expense_limit.value: $3,000 of employment-related expenses for one qualifying individual and $6,000 for two or more — neither indexed

aotc.amount.value: $2,500 per eligible student — 100 percent of the first $2,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses plus 25 percent of the next $2,000 — of which 40 percent is refundable

llc.amount.value: 20 percent of up to $10,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses, a maximum of $2,000 per return rather than per student, entirely non-refundable

edcredits.phaseout.value: modified adjusted gross income of $80,000, or $160,000 on a joint return — not indexed since the IRC § 25A(h) adjustment was struck in 2020

savers.thresholds.value: on a joint return, 50 percent up to $48,500 of adjusted gross income, 20 percent to $52,500, 10 percent to $80,500 and nothing above; head of household $36,375 / $39,375 / $60,375; all others $24,250 / $26,250 / $40,250

adoption.credit.value: qualified adoption expenses up to $17,670, of which $5,120 is refundable, phasing out between $265,080 and $305,080 of modified adjusted gross income
adoption.credit.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.04(1)-(3); IRC § 23(a)(4) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70402(a) — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

energy.credit_terminations.value: the residential clean energy credit ends for expenditures made after 31 December 2025, the energy efficient home improvement credit for property placed in service after that date, and the new clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025

eitc.max_credit.value: $664 with no qualifying child, $4,427 with one, $7,316 with two, and $8,231 with three or more

eitc.earned_income_amount.value: $8,680 with no qualifying child, $13,020 with one, and $18,290 with two or with three or more — the earned income at which the maximum credit is reached

eitc.phaseout.value: on a joint return the credit begins to phase out at $18,140 with no child or $31,160 with any, ending at $19,540 / $58,863 / $65,899 / $70,244 by number of children; for every other filing status the thresholds are $10,860 and $23,890, ending at $19,540 / $51,593 / $58,629 / $62,974
eitc.phaseout.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.06(1), adjusting IRC § 32(b), including the § 32(b)(2)(B) joint-return increase — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

eitc.investment_income_limit.value: $12,200 — above this aggregate of disqualified investment income no credit is allowed at all

eitc.childless_age_range.value: at least 25 and under 65 at the close of the taxable year, tested against either spouse on a joint return, with a principal place of abode in the United States for more than half the year

estimated.required_annual_payment.value: the lesser of 90 percent of the tax shown on this year's return or 100 percent of the tax shown on last year's, rising to 110 percent where last year's adjusted gross income exceeded $150,000, or $75,000 for a married individual filing separately

estimated.installment_share.value: 25 percent of the required annual payment per installment, unless the annualized income installment is lower, in which case the reduction is recaptured in the next installment

estimated.de_minimis.value: no addition to tax where the tax shown on the return, reduced by the IRC § 31 withholding credit, is less than $1,000

refund.eitc_actc_hold.value: no credit or refund may be made before the 15th day of the second month following the close of the taxable year where the earned income credit or the refundable child tax credit is claimed

backup.withholding_rate.value: the fourth lowest rate applicable under IRC § 1(c), which is 24 percent for 2026
backup.withholding_rate.source: IRC § 3406(a)(1); IRC § 1(c) as adjusted by Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3406

gift.annual_exclusion.value: the first $19,000 of gifts to any person, other than gifts of future interests, which are never covered however small

gift.noncitizen_spouse_exclusion.value: $194,000 of gifts to a spouse who is not a United States citizen, again excluding future interests

gift.foreign_gift_reporting.value: aggregate gifts from certain foreign persons above $20,573 received in the taxable year

household.fica_threshold.value: $3,000 of cash wages to any one household employee in the year, at which point 6.2 percent social security and 1.45 percent Medicare apply to all cash wages paid to that employee, matched by the employer
household.fica_threshold.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, reviewed 22 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

household.futa.value: cash wages of more than $1,000 in any calendar quarter of this year or last, on the first $7,000 paid to each household employee, at 6 percent less a credit of up to 5.4 percent for state unemployment contributions
household.futa.source: IRS Topic no. 756, reviewed 22 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

infopenalty.6721.value: $340 per return, reduced to $60 if corrected within 30 days and $130 if corrected by 1 August, with annual caps that differ by the filer's gross receipts — the amounts for returns required to be filed in 2027

intl.6038_penalty.value: $10,000 for each annual accounting period, plus a further $10,000 for each 30-day period beginning 90 days after the Service mails notice, capped at $50,000 of continuation penalty

intl.6677_penalty.value: the greater of $10,000 or 35 percent of the gross reportable amount, with a further penalty if the failure continues more than 90 days after notice
